source_steps.text: Fix x0 and tau>0 and define fcurve as declared. The set Ω is open because positivity is open in ℝ. The extension ũ agrees with the smooth u on Ω, so it is smooth near (x0,tau) by H001. The affine curve r↦(x0,r) lies in Ω near tau and has derivative T. The chain rule therefore gives HasDerivAt fcurve u_t(x0,tau) tau, with u_t defined in D010. For every r in (tau/2,3tau/2), H003 implies ‖fcurve(r)‖²=1.

Apply M005 to fcurve at tau with derivative u_t(x0,tau). It gives derivative 2⟨u(x0,tau),u_t(x0,tau)⟩ for the squared norm. Apply M009 on the real line to r↦‖fcurve(r)‖² and the constant real function 1 at tau: F001 gives equality on an open neighborhood of tau. Its Fréchet derivative is consequently the zero map, since the derivative of a constant is zero. A real HasDerivAt value is its Fréchet derivative evaluated at 1; hence uniqueness gives 2⟨u(x0,tau),u_t(x0,tau)⟩=0. Division by the nonzero real 2 proves tangency.

Choose alpha by existential elimination of H004 at (x0,tau). Substitute its equality into the required inner product. Real inner-product bilinearity and symmetry give ⟨u_t,u_tt-Σ_j∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩=⟨u_t,alpha u⟩=alpha⟨u_t,u⟩=0 by F002, all evaluated at (x0,tau). The result contains no alpha, so the witness is eliminated without choosing a scalar field or assuming any regularity of it. Together with F002 this proves both clauses for arbitrary x0 and tau>0, and universal introduction gives the claimed output.

By H001, ũ is smooth on the open set Ω. Apply M008 with this domain and map to obtain smoothness of its Fréchet derivative field. Evaluation at each fixed direction T or S_j is continuous linear, so composition preserves smoothness and gives smoothness of u_t and ∂_{x_j}u. Apply M008 again to these smooth fields on the same open domain and evaluate at the fixed directions to get smoothness of u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u_t and ∂_{x_jx_j}u. These assertions use only positive-time germs of D005. In the finite-dimensional real Euclidean codomain, inner products and norm squares are finite sums of products of smooth coordinate functions. Finite sums and products preserve smoothness; thus e, each g_j, and all three inner-product terms in the claimed output are smooth. Applying M008 to e and g_j and evaluating at T and S_j also proves smoothness of ∂_t e and ∂_{x_j}g_j. Fixed-time spatial sections of each function are smooth by composition with the affine inclusion of Xn.
Fix tau>0. Since 0<tau/2<3tau/2, H005 at these two endpoints supplies a compact spatial set with u=q outside it at every time in the closed interval.

Choose Cwin from F002 and define Owin. A compact subset of the Euclidean space Xn is closed, so Owin is open and contained in Ω. On Owin, ũ is identically q. Apply M009 at each point of Owin to ũ and the constant map q, whose derivative is zero. Thus its whole derivative field is zero on Owin. Apply M009 again, now to that derivative field and the zero continuous-linear-map-valued function, to obtain zero second derivative there. Evaluation in T and S_j shows that u_t, ∂_{x_j}u, u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u_t and ∂_{x_jx_j}u all vanish on Owin. Consequently e, g_j and the three listed inner-product terms vanish there by their definitions. Since e and g_j are identically zero on this open set, further applications of M009 to e and g_j and the constant scalar zero give ∂_t e=0 and ∂_{x_j}g_j=0 throughout Owin. No conclusion about derivatives at the time endpoints is needed.

For every interior time r, F003 puts the nonzero set of each spatial section inside Cwin. Closure of that nonzero set is still contained in Cwin since Cwin is closed; this closure is tsupport by D014. It is compact as a closed subset of the compact Cwin. Combine this with the joint smoothness in F001. Cwin witnesses all support assertions simultaneously for this tau. The conclusion no longer depends on its private identity; existential elimination and universal introduction for arbitrary tau prove the full claimed output, including all three inner-product terms.

Fix x0 and tau>0, and introduce Vfield,Wfield,Afield,Bfield as declared. H001 implies ũ is smooth on the open Ω. M008 gives a smooth Fréchet derivative field there. Its evaluation at each constant direction is smooth, because evaluation at a fixed vector is continuous linear. Repeating M008 and fixed-vector evaluation shows that Vfield,Wfield,Afield,Bfield and the spatial derivatives of Vfield are smooth on Ω. In particular all are differentiable at (x0,tau). The affine restrictions in time and space are smooth and have derivatives obtained by evaluation in T and S_j by the chain rule. All such curves stay inside Ω near their positive-time base points.

Define Lfield as declared. For every coordinate j, differentiating evaluation at a constant vector gives D_T Wfield_j=(D_T Lfield)[S_j], since Wfield_j=Lfield[S_j]; there is no derivative of the fixed S_j. Similarly D_{S_j}Vfield=(D_{S_j}Lfield)[T]. Apply M007 to ũ at (x0,tau), using F001's C² regularity. Symmetry of its second derivative makes these expressions equal. Thus the mixed derivative needed in the energy calculation is D_T Wfield_j=D_{S_j}Vfield at (x0,tau).

Apply M005 to the time curve r↦Vfield(x0,r) at tau, whose derivative is Afield(x0,tau), and for each j to r↦Wfield_j(x0,r), whose derivative is D_T Wfield_j(x0,tau). These derivatives follow from F001 and the directional definitions. Differentiate the finite sum in D011 and substitute F002. This yields ∂_t e(x0,tau)=2⟨Vfield,Afield⟩(x0,tau)+2Σ_j⟨Wfield_j,D_{S_j}Vfield⟩(x0,tau).

For each j apply M006 on Xn×ℝ to f=Vfield, g=Wfield_j, direction S_j at (x0,tau). Both functions are differentiable there by F001. D012 identifies their inner product with g_j on the positive-time neighborhood, and Bfield_j=D_{S_j}Wfield_j. The product rule gives ∂_{x_j}g_j(x0,tau)=⟨Vfield(x0,tau),Bfield_j(x0,tau)⟩+⟨D_{S_j}Vfield(x0,tau),Wfield_j(x0,tau)⟩.

Subtract twice the finite sum of F004 from F003. Symmetry of the real inner product cancels the terms containing D_{S_j}Vfield. Bilinearity combines the remaining terms into 2⟨Vfield,Afield-Σ_j Bfield_j⟩(x0,tau). The identifications in the declarations make this 2⟨u_t,u_tt-Σ_j∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩(x0,tau), which is zero by the second clause of N001. Hence ∂_t e=2Σ_j∂_{x_j}g_j at this point, with exactly the factor 2. Universal introduction over arbitrary x0 and positive tau proves the claimed output.

Fix tau>0. Instantiate N002 at center time tau and choose its compact Cwin. The time tau belongs to (tau/2,3tau/2). N002 therefore places the topological support of each listed spatial section at tau inside Cwin. Each such support is closed by D014 and so compact as a closed subset of a compact set. Joint smoothness in N002 implies continuity of each fixed-time section by the affine spatial inclusion. This proves continuity and compact support of the sections of e, ∂_t e and ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, as well as, for every coordinate j, of g_j, ∂_{x_j}g_j, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩.

Apply M001 to the three scalar section types e(·,tau), ∂_t e(·,tau) and ⟨u_t(·,tau),u_tt(·,tau)⟩ using F001 with measure dx. For each coordinate j=1,…,n, also apply it to the other four section types in F001 at that j. Each application gives absolute integrability on Xn. The index is universally bound in these four families of applications; no choice of a spatial index is needed for the first three sections.

F002 states exactly the required integrability conclusions at tau. The support witness Cwin does not occur in those conclusions, so eliminate its private identity. Since tau>0 was arbitrary, universal introduction proves all clauses of the claimed output.

Fix tau>0 and define Uwin,Fpar,Dpar as declared. By N002, Fpar and Dpar are jointly continuous on Uwin×Xn after swapping the two coordinates. Smoothness of e gives, for every x∈Xn and r∈Uwin, HasDerivAt (s↦Fpar(s)(x)) Dpar(r)(x) r: the affine time inclusion has derivative T, so D010 identifies its chain-rule derivative with ∂_t e. Every r in Uwin is positive. N004 makes Fpar(r) and Dpar(r) integrable for every such r, and integrability implies almost everywhere strong measurability. In particular Fpar(tau) is integrable and Dpar(tau) is almost everywhere strongly measurable. Uwin is an open neighborhood of tau, so measurability of Fpar(r) holds eventually at tau.

Choose Cwin by N002 at tau; throughout Uwin, both Fpar and Dpar vanish outside this same compact set. Compact subsets of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded. Thus the absolute values of all finitely many coordinates on Cwin have a finite common bound. Enlarging that bound by 1 gives a positive radius with Cwin contained in its closed coordinate cube; if Cwin is empty, any positive radius suffices.

Choose rho by F002 and define Qbox and Lwin. Each closed bounded coordinate interval is compact; their finite product Qbox is compact in Xn. The interval Lwin is compact and lies in Uwin, since tau>0 gives tau/2<3tau/4≤5tau/4<3tau/2. Thus Lwin×Qbox is compact. By F001, the real function (r,x)↦|Dpar(r)(x)| is continuous on this compact set. Its continuous image is bounded, so a nonnegative real bound exists (also when the set is empty).

Choose beta by F003, and define bdom and Iwin. The closed cube Qbox is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure (2rho)^n. The indicator multiple bdom is measurable and its absolute integral is beta(2rho)^n<∞, so bdom is integrable. The interval Iwin is an open neighborhood of tau and is contained in Lwin and Uwin. For x∈Qbox and r∈Iwin, F003 gives |Dpar(r)(x)|≤beta=bdom(x). For x∉Qbox, the inclusion Cwin⊂Qbox implies x∉Cwin, so F002 gives Dpar(r)(x)=0=bdom(x). Thus the bound holds for every x and every r∈Iwin, which also implies the single almost-everywhere assertion with all r in this same neighborhood. F001 supplies the time derivative for every x and every r∈Iwin.

Apply M002 with spatial measure dx, F=Fpar, D=Dpar, base time tau, neighborhood Iwin and bound bdom. F001 gives eventual section measurability, base integrability and derivative-section measurability; F004 gives the neighborhood, the integrable bound and both universally quantified pointwise conditions, hence their almost-everywhere forms. The theorem concludes integrability of Dpar(tau) and HasDerivAt (r↦∫_{Xn}Fpar(r)(x) dx) (∫_{Xn}Dpar(tau)(x) dx) tau.

By D011 and D013, the integral time function in F005 is exactly the total representation of E, and its restriction to positive times is the desired energy. The section integrability already instantiated in F001 ensures these are finite Lebesgue integrals for times in Uwin, a neighborhood of tau. Dpar(tau)(x)=∂_t e(x,tau) since tau>0. Restriction to the open positive-time domain preserves this derivative, so F005 gives every clause of the claimed output for this tau. The conclusion contains none of Cwin,rho,beta or the auxiliary windows; eliminate their witnesses and universally quantify tau. No behavior at zero is asserted.

Fix tau>0 and a coordinate j0 and define gspace. N002 makes gspace smooth by restriction along the affine map x↦(x,tau), hence globally C¹. Its topological support is compact: N002 at center time tau contains it in a compact spatial set, and tsupport is closed. The same affine inclusion has derivative h↦(h,0). Therefore by the chain rule, for every x∈Xn, Dgspace(x)[b_{j0}]=∂_{x_{j0}}g_{j0}(x,tau), with exactly the directional interpretation D006–D010. These facts require no hypotheses beyond N002's smoothness and support statements.

Apply E004 with g=gspace and the constant spatial vector v=b_{j0}. F001 verifies its C¹ and compact-support premises. It gives integrability of Dgspace(·)[b_{j0}] and its zero integral. Using F001's pointwise derivative identification yields ∫_{Xn}∂_{x_{j0}}g_{j0}(x,tau) dx=0. The result is independent of the notation gspace; since j0 was arbitrary, this proves the zero integral for every coordinate.

At time tau, N003 is the pointwise equality ∂_t e(x,tau)=2Σ_j∂_{x_j}g_j(x,tau). N004 supplies integrability of the left side and of each derivative on the right. Linearity of the Lebesgue integral for finite sums and real scalar multiplication therefore applies and gives ∫_{Xn}∂_t e(x,tau) dx=2Σ_j∫_{Xn}∂_{x_j}g_j(x,tau) dx=0 by F002. This is finite integral linearity, so no infinite interchange is involved. Since tau>0 was arbitrary, universal introduction proves the claimed output.

Fix arbitrary tau>0. N004 states that e(·,tau) is Lebesgue integrable, so D013's E(tau) is the finite actual integral required by the target. N005 gives a derivative of E at tau with value ∫_{Xn}∂_t e(x,tau) dx. N006 identifies precisely this integral as zero. Substitution therefore gives HasDerivAt E 0 tau on the open positive-time domain. By the definition and uniqueness of a derivative this entails differentiability there and E'(tau)=0. The formula for e in D011 is |u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|², and D010 gives the stated Frobenius and componentwise Laplacian normalizations, with no factor 1/2. Since tau>0 was arbitrary this is all clauses of the target, including integrability at every positive time and no assertion at time zero.

import Mathlib
open MeasureTheory Filter Set
open scoped Topology BigOperators ContDiff

abbrev WMX (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
abbrev WMZ (n : ℕ) := WMX n × ℝ
def WMOmega (n : ℕ) : Set (WMZ n) := {z | 0 < z.2}
def WMT (n : ℕ) : WMZ n := (0, 1)
noncomputable def WMBasis (n : ℕ) (j : Fin n) : WMX n :=
  EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ j
noncomputable def WMS (n : ℕ) (j : Fin n) : WMZ n := (WMBasis n j, 0)
noncomputable def WMV {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (z : WMZ n) : WMX m :=
  fderiv ℝ u z (WMT n)
noncomputable def WMW {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (j : Fin n) (z : WMZ n) : WMX m :=
  fderiv ℝ u z (WMS n j)
noncomputable def WMA {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (z : WMZ n) : WMX m :=
  fderiv ℝ (WMV u) z (WMT n)
noncomputable def WMB {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (j : Fin n) (z : WMZ n) : WMX m :=
  fderiv ℝ (WMW u j) z (WMS n j)
noncomputable def WMMixed {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (j : Fin n) (z : WMZ n) : WMX m :=
  fderiv ℝ (WMV u) z (WMS n j)
noncomputable def WME {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (z : WMZ n) : ℝ :=
  if 0 < z.2 then ‖WMV u z‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖WMW u j z‖ ^ 2 else 0
noncomputable def WMG {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (j : Fin n) (z : WMZ n) : ℝ :=
  if 0 < z.2 then inner ℝ (WMV u z) (WMW u j z) else 0
noncomputable def WMET {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (z : WMZ n) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ (WME u) z (WMT n)
noncomputable def WMGX {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (j : Fin n) (z : WMZ n) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ (WMG u j) z (WMS n j)
noncomputable def WMEnergy {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : WMX n, WME u (x, t)
inductive WMTerm (n : ℕ) where
  | density | densityTime | kineticPair
  | flux (j : Fin n) | fluxSpace (j : Fin n)
  | mixedPair (j : Fin n) | laplacePair (j : Fin n)
noncomputable def WMField {n m : ℕ} (u : WMZ n → WMX m) : WMTerm n → WMZ n → ℝ
  | .density => WME u
  | .densityTime => WMET u
  | .kineticPair => fun z => inner ℝ (WMV u z) (WMA u z)
  | .flux j => WMG u j
  | .fluxSpace j => WMGX u j
  | .mixedPair j => fun z => inner ℝ (WMW u j z) (WMMixed u j z)
  | .laplacePair j => fun z => inner ℝ (WMV u z) (WMB u j z)

H005 retains exactly one compact spatial set for each closed interval 0<s<t, uniformly for all its times and outside spatial points. Restricting any such total u to positive time gives the original data; conversely any original map extends by q at nonpositive times, and local equality on the open domain preserves all derivatives and these assumptions. The standard basis Fin n is a coordinate relabeling and the Euclidean norm gives exactly the Frobenius sum of spatial squares, with no factor 1/2. WME is the specified density on positive time and WMEnergy its volume integral; the integrability conjunct ensures this is the actual finite Lebesgue integral. For every t>0, HasDerivAt (WMEnergy u) 0 t is equivalent to differentiability and deriv (WMEnergy u) t=0, by uniqueness and the derivative of a differentiable real function. Ordinary differentiation of the total energy at t agrees in both directions with differentiation on the original open positive-time interval, since a neighborhood of t stays positive. No assertion at t=0 or negative times is made, and no extra hypothesis is added by the representation.

representation: Use EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), which are PiLp 2 spaces: the inner product is the sum of coordinate products and the norm is Euclidean, not the sup norm on an ordinary function space. The coordinate index Fin n relabels 1,…,n by 0,…,n−1. WMBasis is EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ, whose inspected application is the single-coordinate vector with value 1. Volume is the standard Euclidean Lebesgue measure. The product WMZ n carries the standard product norm; this changes neither the topology nor the Fréchet derivatives of Euclidean maps. The parameter u is an arbitrary total extension of the positive-time map; all smoothness and sphere/PDE assumptions are restricted to the open WMOmega n. WMV,WMW,WMA,WMB,WMMixed are fderiv ℝ evaluated at the constant time or spatial directions; total fderiv asserts no differentiability by definition. Density WME and flux WMG are zero at nonpositive times; their derivatives elsewhere need no off-domain interpretation. WMEnergy is the real Bochner integral of density for volume. Integrability is exported separately, so a totalized integral never supplies finiteness. The smoothness symbol ∞ is the infinite differentiability order in ℕ∞ω, not analytic order ω; C¹ in E004 and the flux interface is order 1. For real Hessian symmetry minSmoothness ℝ 2=2, so no analyticity is required. WMTerm/WMField package exactly e,e_t,⟨u_t,u_tt⟩ and the four j-indexed families g_j,∂_j g_j,⟨∂_j u,∂_j u_t⟩,⟨u_t,∂_jj u⟩.
